title: Federated Edge Tenant Provisioning and Control Plane Contract
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the tenant provisioning contract and operational runbook for federated edge and VPC control planes that Redwood ships with Private deployments. It is intended for SREs, Field Operators, Solutions Engineers, and partner integrators.

Goals

- Provide a repeatable, testable provisioning flow for tenants across hybrid topologies (cloud VPCs + on-prem/edge nodes).
- Define control-plane APIs, expected telemetry, and operator responsibilities.
- Specify SLOs, acceptance tests, rollback windows, and forensic evidence requirements for tenant lifecycle events.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to Private deployments with a delegated control plane or federated control plane topology.
- Assumes operator access to tenant network, KMS boundary, and a host agent on edge appliances.
- Not a replacement for full security onboarding checklists; see customer-specific compliance pages for regulatory artifacts.

Key definitions

- Tenant: Logical namespace representing a customer workload and associated keys, quotas, and models.
- Federated control plane: A model where a central Redwood management plane coordinates with a customer-local control plane (edge or VPC) for tenant lifecycle and telemetry aggregation.
- Operator: Field engineer or customer operator responsible for running on-prem agents and executing handoff/rollback steps.

Service-level expectations

- Provisioning completion: 95th percentile <= 6 minutes for standard tenant rollouts; median <= 90s for pre-provisioned tenants.
- KV cache warm window: 90% of requests receive warm cache within 15 minutes of first production traffic.
- Telemetry delivery: Control plane events must be available to the central telemetry gateway within 60s for healthy links.

Ownership and run ownership matrix

| Activity | Primary Owner | Secondary Owner | Escalation path |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tenant create request acceptance | Solutions Engineering | Field Operator | SRE oncall -> Product Ops |
| Edge image attestation | Field Operator | Security Team | Security oncall |
| KMS boundary verification | Customer Security | Redwood Security | Legal/Security escalation |
| Post-provision smoke test | Operator | SRE | SRE oncall |

Provisioning workflow (step-by-step)

1. Preflight checks (automated)
   - Validate connectivity to Redwood registry and telemetry gateway.
   - Verify KMS endpoints, service account scopes, and ACLs.
   - Confirm hardware SKU & GPU firmware match the compatibility matrix.

2. Tenant declaration
   - Customer or solutions engineer submits a TenantDeclaration JSON to /api/v1/tenants with fields: name, region_hints, kms_boundary, operator_contact.
   - Example (curl):

     curl -X POST https://controlplane.example/api/v1/tenants \\n       -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \\n       -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n       -d '{"name":"acme-payments","region_hints":["eu-west-1","onprem-site-1"],"kms_boundary":"projects/acme-kms/locations/global/keyRings/ring1/cryptoKeys/key1","operator_contact":"ops@acme.example"}'

3. Operator handshake and image attestation
   - Operator runs attestation: `redwood-agent attest --image sha256:... --policy /etc/attestation/policy.json`
   - Attestation report is posted to /api/v1/attestations with link to signed manifest.

4. Control plane registration
   - Federated control plane posts its endpoint and cert bundle via the ControlPlaneRegister API. Central plane verifies operator signature and stores the endpoint in the tenant manifest.

5. Capability negotiation
   - Central plane returns the allowed model profiles, quantization capabilities, and routing preferences.
   - Operator can accept or request an alternate set within 30 minutes. If no response, central plane defaults to conservative profiles (no preemption, single model variant).

6. Image rollout and smoke tests
   - Central plane triggers a staged rollout to edge nodes with canary fraction=5%.
   - Smoke tests executed: generation latency, KV cache reconciliation, telemetry heartbeat, basic auth checks.

7. Production cutover and telemetry validation
   - After smoke success, gradual traffic ramp (10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) with 5–10 minute observation windows.
   - Telemetry must show stable token cost and latencies within +/-10% of pre-provision baseline.

Operator checklist (pre-provision)

- [ ] Confirm operator IAM key has least privilege access.
- [ ] Run `redwood-agent preflight --check-all` and resolve failures.
- [ ] Verify local time sync (NTP) and TPM attestation status.
- [ ] Confirm firewall egress rules allow telemetry and image registry access on required ports (443, 5222 for internal agent comms).

Configuration table (minimum valid tenant manifest)

| Field | Required | Description | Example |
|---|---:|---|---|
| name | yes | Tenant identifier (dns-friendly) | acme-payments |
| region_hints | yes | Preferred regions for model fanout | ["onprem-site-1","eu-west-1"] |
| kms_boundary | yes | KMS resource path for tenant keys | projects/acme-kms/... |
| quota_profile | no | Baseline QPS and burst allowances | small/medium/large |
| allowed_models | no | Model family and required quantization | ["rwkv-7b-int8","redwood-2-13b-q4"] |

Acceptance tests and automated checks

- Acceptance test harness includes: smoke_gen.sh (generation end-to-end), kv_reconciliation_check, telemetry_latency_check.
- Local operator must run acceptance-suite with `./acceptance-suite --tenant acme-payments --mode remote` and attach logs to the tenant record.

Rollback and emergency procedures

1. Synchronous rollback (immediate)
   - Triggered when a canary fails critical smoke tests or latency SLOs exceed threshold for 2 consecutive windows.
   - Command: `POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenant}/actions -d '{"action":"rollback","target":"previous-stable"}'`
   - Operator verifies rollback: check artifact_digest matches previous stable, KV cache flush may be required using `redwood-agent kv-flush --tenant acme-payments`.

2. Forensic preservation
   - Before destructive rollback, capture: artifact manifests, attestation bundles, NTP-synced logs (last 1 hour), and network captures (if permitted). Store evidence in the tenant evidence bucket with tamper-evident metadata.

3. Failed rollback and operator escape hatch
   - If rollback fails to rehydrate previous stable, operator can trigger a binary fallback: start an isolated fallback service on dedicated instance pool and route 100% traffic to fallback pool while investigation proceeds.

Upgrade window and compatibility gates

- Upgrades to agent or control plane components must pass a compatibility matrix for: image format, artifact schema version, model artifact manifest version, and KV cache format.
- Gate checks (automated): smoke tests, backward-compatible API verification, and canary traffic validation.
- Recommended upgrade window: 02:00–06:00 local site time with a 2-hour observation window post-100% ramp.

Observability and telemetry contract

- Required control-plane events (must be emitted within 60s): TENANT_CREATE, CONTROLPLANE_REGISTER, ATTESTATION_UPLOAD, SMOKE_TEST_RESULT, ROLLBACK_INIT, ROLLBACK_COMPLETE.
- Each event must include: tenant_id, artifact_digest, operator_id, timestamp (ISO8601), and correlation_id.

Example event JSON (flattened):

{
  "event_type": "SMOKE_TEST_RESULT",
  "tenant_id": "acme-payments",
  "artifact_digest": "sha256:abcd...",
  "operator_id": "ops@acme.example",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-30T03:15:12Z",
  "correlation_id": "cf4a-12b3-...",
  "result": "PASS"
}

Security and compliance notes

- KMS boundaries must be enforced by customer-managed KMS in restricted deployments. Redwood will only persist key references; no raw keys are stored in the central plane.
- Signed attestation bundles are required for field-installable images. Operators should use hardware-backed attestation where available.

Operator training and runbook drills

- Quarterly drills: simulated canary failure, emergency rollback, and forensic evidence collection.
- Game-day checklist sample:
  1. Inject controlled canary failure.
  2. Observe detection and automated rollback trigger.
  3. Execute forensic snapshot and validate evidence upload.

Appendix A — Example tenant manifest YAML

---
name: acme-payments
region_hints:
  - onprem-site-1
  - eu-west-1
kms_boundary: projects/acme-kms/locations/global/keyRings/ring1/cryptoKeys/key1
quota_profile: medium
allowed_models:
  - rwkv-7b-int8
  - redwood-2-13b-q4

Appendix B — Useful CLI commands

- redwood-agent preflight --check-all
- redwood-agent attest --image <digest> --policy /etc/attestation/policy.json
- redwood-agent kv-flush --tenant <tenant>
- curl -X POST https://controlplane.example/api/v1/tenants -d '{...}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
